Below is a one-line patch which makes the Smalltalk “string” pattern allow an empty body (i.e. change the inner + to *).  With this change, `''` will be recognized as a valid string literal.

```javascript
### components/prism-smalltalk.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'string': /\'(?:\'\'|[^\'])+\'/,
=======
    'string': /\'(?:\'\'|[^\'])*\'/,
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the root cause and fix:

1. **Symptom**  
   In the screenshots you can see that the empty Smalltalk string `''` is not highlighted as a string at all (no green), whereas longer strings like `'foo'` are.

2. **Cause**  
   The original regex  
     /\'(?:\'\'|[^\'])+\'/  
   requires at least one repetition of either a doubled quote (`''`) or a non-quote character.  It will not match `''` because there is zero content inside, so the `+` fails to match.

3. **Fix**  
   By changing the `+` to `*` we allow zero or more repetitions of the interior pattern.  Now `/\'(?:\'\'|[^\'])*\'/` will match:
     • `''`  
     • `'''` (a quote in the middle, written as `''''`)  
     • any other valid Smalltalk string, including the empty one.
